title: Relative finite Hilbert groupoids and their unramified lci subcategories
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of stacks in groupoids on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and object descent is effective. For each integer $d\geq1$ define $\mathcal H_d(F)(T)$ to have objects $(Z\xrightarrow{p}T,y,x,\alpha)$, where $p$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$, and $\alpha:y|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$. An arrow over $g:T\to T'$ consists of a cartesian scheme map $h:Z\to Z'$ (so $Z\simeq T\times_{T'}Z'$), isomorphisms $b:y\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*y'$ and $a:x\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*x'$, satisfying $F(a)\circ\alpha=(h^*\alpha')\circ(b|_Z)$ under the pullback identifications. Composition is composition of these maps and isomorphisms; pullback is scheme base change and cartesian pullback of objects [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $p_d:\mathcal H_d(F)\to\mathcal Y$ for the functor remembering $y$. Here $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(V,T)$, regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid. The $2$-fibre product $h_T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ has, over $V$, triples $(t:V\to T,\xi\in\mathcal X(V),\beta:t^*y\xrightarrow{\sim}F(\xi))$, with arrows given by isomorphisms of $\xi$ compatible with $\beta$. Say that $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every $T$ and $y$, this fibred groupoid is equivalent to the discrete fibred groupoid of an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Fix such a representative when it exists. The object $(p,x,\alpha)$ over $Z$ then specifies the map $u:Z\to X_y$ over $T$. When $F$ is additionally flat and locally of finite presentation, meaning that every $X_y\to T$ has these scheme properties on etale scheme charts in the sense of the next sentences [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], define $\mathcal L_d(F)$ as the full subcategory of $\mathcal H_d(F)$ where $u$ is unramified and a local complete intersection morphism. A space map $v:A\to B$ has one of these scheme properties when there exist a surjective etale scheme chart $V\to B$ and a surjective etale scheme chart $U\to A\times_BV$ such that the composite scheme map $U\to V$ has it. Here etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism]. In particular, unramified means unramified in the sense of [def-weil-unramified-morphism] (locally of finite type with open diagonal, equivalently with zero relative Kahler differentials); local complete intersection means that locally on the source the scheme map factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] followed by a smooth scheme map [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with the closed immersion's ideal locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Here a sequence $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ in a ring $B$ is Koszul-regular when the complex with terms $\bigwedge^q B^r$ and differential $e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_q}\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^q(-1)^{j-1}f_{i_j}e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\widehat{e_{i_j}}\cdots\wedge e_{i_q}$ is exact in every positive degree; the empty sequence is allowed. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space].
